results.reason: The graph captures the booking and the team's reason, but attaches “tomorrow morning” to “like” and “short” to “planning.” Both qualify the meeting being booked.
The farm's “with” relation reaches only the shed. The graph uses apposition for the other entities where the source coordinates all four as things the farm has.
The draw imperative specifies a big, ringed planet and places the drawing to the left of the indicated lake.
The slice labels are the subject of “want,” the “on” relation links them to Budget split, and the complement specifies a medium distance.
The graph gives both step counts, but “back” scopes over the shared “take” predicate, whose object includes both step groups. The source limits “back” to the first two steps.
The graph preserves the “can you” question and identifies the caps, but makes “bigger” a modifier of the error bars. The caps are what should become bigger.
The give imperative identifies “me” as the recipient and a greenhouse next to the house as the object.
The reverse imperative takes “the last thing” as its object and preserves “last” as the qualifier.
The graph identifies the dots on the dashed line, but attaches “wider” to the relation with the revenue trend. “Wider” describes the desired state of the dots.
